claims.text: The mental model is: skills are reusable instructions, templates, and domain expertise; actions are tool calls that read from or write to systems; MCP is an open protocol for exposing tools and data to AI apps and agents; and agents are the governed workflow wrapper that packages skills, tools, and knowledge together.
Use custom actions when you need deterministic execution against an internal API, legacy system, or proprietary workflow.
MCP is an open standard for connecting AI assistants to external data sources and tools.
Glean can act as both an MCP server and an MCP host.
For partners, MCP means faster integrations, less lock-in, and easier reuse across hosts such as Cursor, Claude, ChatGPT, and VS Code.
Remote MCP servers are fully supported for Assistant.
In Agents, MCP-backed tools are available in Plan and Execute mode and in auto mode.
MCP tools are not available as individual single-step selections in Agent Builder.
Custom actions are org-defined automations for cases where built-in actions and action packs are not enough.
Custom actions fit internal APIs or services Glean does not support out of the box, legacy or in-house systems, and approvals, validation, or custom business logic before writing to a system.
Builders add a custom action as a step in Agent Builder, and its inputs can be fixed values, user inputs, or AI-predicted values.
Custom actions can be combined with By Glean and By datasource actions in the same workflow.
An example custom action is an internal IT onboarding action that creates a request and returns a request ID plus a link.
BLD-102 explains actions, MCP, architecture choices, and when to use each approach.
BLD-103 is a hands-on workshop building actions and MCP-backed flows.
